description: Seeded non-player character, creature, entity, monster, otherworldly being, and high-clearance Eldritch threat generator using a 1-10 Power Classification system.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 1 — Insignificant Mundane
powerLevels.scale: Tiny animals, vermin, insects, harmless swarms, ordinary pets, or creatures whose importance is symbolic, environmental, or emotional rather than combat-scale.
powerLevels.baseline: 1-2 dice if a roll is relevant; usually scene texture, evidence, nuisance, or vulnerability.
powerLevels.narrative: A Power 1 creature can matter, but it is not a combat threat unless the environment makes it one.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 2 — Ordinary Civilian Scale
powerLevels.scale: Ordinary humans, domestic animals, weak predators, untrained witnesses, support staff, and frightened people without exceptional capability.
powerLevels.baseline: 2-3 dice for routine actions; low stress tolerance under supernatural pressure.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 2 beings create moral pressure, social stakes, evidence, witnesses, dependencies, or liabilities.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 3 — Trained Mundane
powerLevels.scale: Professionals, guards, responders, trained animals, gang members, and competent civilians with equipment and discipline.
powerLevels.baseline: 3-5 dice in trained tasks; dangerous to ordinary people but not prepared for true supernatural escalation.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 3 opponents complicate public scenes and punish carelessness while remaining fundamentally mundane.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 4 — Capable Field Actor
powerLevels.scale: Veteran professionals, Blacklight staff, occult-aware civilians, skilled criminals, dangerous animals, and newly awakened supernatural actors.
powerLevels.baseline: 5-7 dice in core competencies; may possess one exceptional trick, limited supernatural contact, or excellent equipment.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 4 is the first level where an NPC can drive a scene instead of only complicating it.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 5 — Standard Operative Threat
powerLevels.scale: Baseline player-scale professionals, active BlackLight operatives, trained hunters, capable supernatural beings, and dangerous monsters.
powerLevels.baseline: 7-9 dice in focused strengths; credible threat to a starting team member or useful ally in field operations.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 5 is a fair serious NPC scale: not a god, not scenery, and not something players should ignore.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 6 — Elite or Major Supernatural
powerLevels.scale: Elite operatives, veteran supernatural entities, major monsters, senior technomancers, professional killers, and beings with several strong capabilities.
powerLevels.baseline: 9-11 dice in major actions; can dominate ordinary scenes and force team coordination.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 6 beings change how a scene is approached. They are not impossible, but they punish lazy planning.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 7 — Regional Apex
powerLevels.scale: Local supernatural rulers, ancient hunters, elite machine intelligences, large alien remnants, pack champions, court agents, named monsters, and restricted Eldritch field hazards.
powerLevels.baseline: 11-14 dice or several scene-shaping tools; may require preparation, leverage, or environmental advantage.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 7 entities are problems with territory, followers, rules, habits, and consequences.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 8 — Strategic Entity
powerLevels.scale: City-scale powers, major spirits, sovereign monsters, distributed machine intelligences, old court champions, intrusion vessels, and entities that reshape operations around themselves.
powerLevels.baseline: 14-18 dice where dice still matter; direct confrontation should require narrative positioning.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 8 threats are campaign arcs. They are negotiated with, trapped, exposed, redirected, or fought only under carefully built conditions.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 9 — Reality-Scale Power
powerLevels.scale: Deities, elder sovereigns, extradimensional authorities, primal patrons, old watchers, major incursion phenomena, and entities whose attention can alter nations, species, or metaphysical structures.
powerLevels.baseline: Narrative-tier opposition; rolls usually determine access, survival, leverage, or consequence rather than defeat.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 9 entities are not boss fights unless the campaign is already about impossible alliances, loopholes, and catastrophic stakes.

powerLevels.label: Power Class 10 — Extravagant Limited Sovereign
powerLevels.scale: Charles-tier and beyond: extradimensional matrioska-brain intelligences, quantum-wormhole and black-hole tunneling actors, entities able to exert electromagnetic influence across the dimension of play, and beings capable of continent, stellar, existential, or cognitohazardous feats while still possessing strange boundaries.
powerLevels.baseline: Do not treat as a normal stat block. Define permissions, limits, domains, costs, blind spots, prohibitions, clearance restrictions, and what lesser beings can meaningfully influence.
powerLevels.narrative: Power 10 beings can perform extravagant all-powerful feats, but the story depends on what they cannot do, what they are not allowed to do, what costs too much, what they misunderstand, what makes them flinch, or what BlackLight refuses to let mortal staff know.

highSecurityClearanceScales.label: E-3 Ritual Evidence Handler
highSecurityClearanceScales.generatorUse: May generate cult fragments, low-level intrusion creatures, contaminated artifacts, and field evidence. Direct entity descriptions remain redacted.

highSecurityClearanceScales.label: E-4 Binder Liaison
highSecurityClearanceScales.generatorUse: May generate Binder-adjacent creatures, cult guardians, pact-marked victims, and sanitized breach symptoms.

highSecurityClearanceScales.label: E-5 Intrusion Analyst
highSecurityClearanceScales.generatorUse: May generate cross-cult patterns, named intrusion creatures, leadership assets, and restricted manifestation profiles.

highSecurityClearanceScales.label: E-6 Hazard Custodian
highSecurityClearanceScales.generatorUse: May generate quarantine vault entities, high-risk artifacts, live hazards, and controlled unsanitized encounter shells.

highSecurityClearanceScales.label: E-7 Director-Level Eldritch Authority
highSecurityClearanceScales.generatorUse: May generate incident command threats, cult leadership, strategic entities, and high-cost containment failures.

highSecurityClearanceScales.label: E-8 Charles-Restricted / Non-Mortal Review
highSecurityClearanceScales.generatorUse: May generate only sanitized aliases for sovereign or entity-core phenomena. Full entity truth is never printed into normal generator output.

categories.label: Human Vigil, Hunter, or Occult-Aware Mortal
Restricted Eldritch Cultist or Cell Operator
capabilityTags: can trigger a prepared ritual fragment
categories.restrictedHandling: Generated cultists are safe to brief as organizational threats. Do not infer full entity truth from their doctrine.

categories.label: High-Clearance Eldritch Intrusion Creature
categories.restrictedHandling: Treat as a field hazard. The creature may be described, contained, and fought; its true metaphysical anatomy remains redacted.

categories.label: Eldritch Servitor or Construct
examples: placement drone made of borrowed limbs
categories.restrictedHandling: Servitor files require incident-specific access and post-contact exposure review.

categories.label: Eldritch Cognitohazard Manifestation
categories.restrictedHandling: Generator output must remain sanitized. Full description is intentionally withheld because the record itself may be hazardous.

categories.label: Eldritch Vessel or Incursion Host
categories.restrictedHandling: Vessels are not automatically disposable monsters. They may be victims, leaders, evidence, or catastrophic doors.

categories.label: Charles-Restricted Apex Eldritch Incursion
examples: Hunger event with a mouth for a city
categories.restrictedHandling: Use as campaign structure, not a random fight. Printed output remains a safe placeholder, never the full entity.
